rules.title: Governance catalog must be structurally and referentially valid
rules.description: The canonical catalog and deterministic check registry must validate, use unique identifiers, preserve approval authority, and contain no orphan check links.

scope.description: The versioned governance catalog, registry, and schemas.

evidence_requirements: Schema validation and catalog-to-check referential integrity results.

approval.rationale: Approved as the fail-closed catalog foundation.

rules.title: Codex must expose the complete governed role catalog
rules.description: The supported Codex runtime must declare exactly the eight governed roles required by the canonical orchestration contract.

scope.description: Codex agent templates in source, project, and global layouts.

evidence_requirements: Normalized Codex role set matched to the canonical governed role inventory.

approval.rationale: Approved for the Codex-only governed role catalog.

rules.title: Independent reviewers must remain report-only
rules.description: Architecture, quality, and security reviewers must not receive write capability or implementation ownership.

scope.description: Codex architecture, quality, and security reviewer declarations.

evidence_requirements: Reviewer capability declarations and explicit report-only instructions.

approval.rationale: Approved to preserve independent Codex review ownership.

rules.title: Review handoffs must use the validated governance envelope
rules.description: Reviewers must emit one pure JSON result with correct role, runtime, gate type, bounded evidence, and referential integrity.

scope.description: Codex structured review prompts, schema validation, and fail-closed pipeline integration.

evidence_requirements: Codex prompt contracts, schema validation, and fail-closed pipeline integration.

approval.rationale: Approved to fail closed on invalid Codex independent review handoffs.

rules.title: Pipeline dependencies and failed gates must be enforced
rules.description: Every declared dependency must exist and precede its consumer, cycles are forbidden, and dependent stages must not continue after invalid or failed gates.

scope.description: All declared Codex pipeline strategies and hard rules.

evidence_requirements: Dependency existence, ordering, acyclicity, and fail-closed policy evidence.

approval.rationale: Approved as the deterministic sequencing gate.

rules.title: Review findings must return through remediation and revalidation
rules.description: A finding routes to the implementer, deterministic checks rerun, and the originating gate revalidates the correction.

scope.description: Governed review remediation flows.

evidence_requirements: A linked implementation handoff, repeated deterministic result, and originating gate decision.

approval.rationale: Approved with warning effect until execution persistence can prove the loop occurred.

rules.title: The main session is the orchestration authority
rules.description: The active main session selects strategy, enforces sequencing, and integrates results; an orchestrator subagent is not the normal authority path.

scope.description: All multi-agent execution strategies.

evidence_requirements: The selected strategy and actor ownership for every governed stage.

approval.rationale: Approved in the governance responsibility baseline.

rules.title: Role capabilities must match approved ownership
rules.description: Explorer and planner remain read-only, documentator writes only specifications, implementer owns code changes, and independent reviewers remain report-only.

scope.description: Codex role declarations and capabilities.

evidence_requirements: Role sandboxes and prompt ownership constraints for Codex.

approval.rationale: Approved in the Codex-only responsibility design.

rules.title: Architecture review applies to architecture-sensitive changes
rules.description: Architecture review is required for material changes to boundaries, dependency direction, public contracts, persistence, integrations, or shared architecture decisions.

scope.description: Changes that may affect architecture-sensitive surfaces.

evidence_requirements: A recorded applicability decision tied to the changed contracts, boundaries, persistence, or integrations.

approval.rationale: Approved with warning effect because applicability still requires contextual judgment.

rules.title: Active security validation requires explicit authorization
rules.description: Security review is passive by default; intrusive, destructive, or high-risk validation requires explicit human or parent authorization before execution.

scope.description: Active or high-risk security validation.

evidence_requirements: The explicit authorization reference and the bounded active validation scope.

approval.rationale: Approved as the Codex active security authorization boundary.

rules.title: Testable implementation follows strict TDD
rules.description: The implementer demonstrates RED, implements the minimum GREEN change, refactors safely, and reports final test evidence.

scope.description: Testable code and contract changes.

evidence_requirements: Failing regression evidence before implementation and passing evidence after implementation.

approval.rationale: Approved with warning effect because testability and RED evidence still require review judgment.

rules.title: Failed or invalid gates stop dependent work
rules.description: A required gate that is failed, invalid, unresolved, or not run prevents dependent stages from continuing. Pipeline configuration provides partial static coverage; execution behavior remains review-owned without persistence.

scope.description: All required governance gates and their dependent stages.

evidence_requirements: The predecessor gate result and proof that dependent work did not start; pipeline_dependency_order supplies only static policy coverage.

approval.rationale: Approved as a blocking execution rule with partial static pipeline coverage.

rules.title: Deterministic checks take precedence over agent opinion
rules.description: Objective checks own automatable pass or fail decisions and cannot be overridden by an agent assertion without an approved exception.

scope.description: Rules with an objective deterministic verification path.

evidence_requirements: The deterministic result and any applicable human-approved exception.

approval.rationale: Approved in the governance responsibility baseline.

rules.title: Governance evidence is bounded and privacy-safe
rules.description: Evidence contains structured summaries and references, never raw unbounded output, secrets, credentials, PII, payloads, or raw trace identifiers.

scope.description: All governance evidence and validation errors.

evidence_requirements: Schema-conformant evidence with explicit redaction metadata and sanitized validation errors.

approval.rationale: Approved as the evidence safety boundary.

rules.title: Candidate or unverified findings never block
rules.description: A proposed rule, unverified finding, or unreproduced finding cannot produce a blocking gate effect.

scope.description: Rule status, finding validation, and effective gate decisions.

evidence_requirements: The approved rule status and verified reproduced finding state for each blocking decision.

approval.rationale: Approved as a fail-closed blocking eligibility constraint.

rules.title: Only human authority approves policy and exceptions
rules.description: Only the user or a designated human authority can approve, modify, deprecate, or except governance rules.

scope.description: Rule approval, lifecycle changes, and exceptions.

evidence_requirements: A human producer and traceable approval reference.

approval.rationale: Approved as the governance authority boundary.

rules.title: Governance exceptions have a bounded lifecycle
rules.description: An exception records its rule, scope, reason, owner, human approval, and expiry or review boundary before it can affect enforcement.

scope.description: All governance rule exceptions.

evidence_requirements: A schema-valid active exception linked to an existing rule and human approval.

approval.rationale: Approved as the exception lifecycle contract.

rules.title: Checks and deterministic rules remain linked
rules.description: Each registered check references an existing rule and each deterministic rule references its registered check. Catalog integrity currently supplies the automated coverage under its own rule identity.

scope.description: The canonical rule catalog and deterministic check registry.

evidence_requirements: Bidirectional catalog and registry integrity; governance_catalog_integrity provides current partial automation.

approval.rationale: Approved without a second registry entry to preserve one check per rule.

rules.title: Project and global installation preserve governance parity
rules.description: Project-scoped and global Codex installation copy equivalent governance schemas, catalog, registry, prompts, and pipeline contracts.

scope.description: Node and shell Codex installer outputs.

evidence_requirements: Temporary project and global installations with byte-equivalent governance contracts.

approval.rationale: Approved as the installation parity contract.

rules.title: Tracked JavaScript and shell source must be syntactically valid
rules.description: Every tracked JavaScript and shell source file in the evaluated repository must pass the package-owned syntax checks.

scope.description: Tracked JavaScript and shell source files in the target repository.

evidence_requirements: Bounded counts and normalized syntax-check outcome without raw command output.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking executor in Issue #8.

rules.title: The repository test suite must complete successfully
rules.description: The package-owned test executor must run the repository test suite without recursively invoking the full engineering gate runner.

scope.description: The target repository test suite executed with the package-owned fixed command.

evidence_requirements: Bounded test command outcome and exit classification.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking executor in Issue #8.

rules.title: Production dependencies must pass the package vulnerability audit
rules.description: The fixed production-only npm audit must complete trustworthily with no reported production dependency vulnerability.

scope.description: Production npm dependencies declared by the target repository.

evidence_requirements: Normalized vulnerability counts or a bounded infrastructure reason code.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking executor in Issue #8.

rules.title: The npm package must contain every required runner asset
rules.description: A script-free npm dry run must complete and include the CLI, runner, schemas, registry, governance, and installer assets required by installed layouts.

scope.description: The npm package dry-run surface of the target repository.

evidence_requirements: Bounded package file counts and normalized missing-asset identifiers.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking executor in Issue #8.

rules.title: Retired runtime surfaces and forbidden references must remain absent
rules.description: Tracked package source must not reintroduce retired runtime implementations, compatibility surfaces, vendor references, or obsolete managed layouts.

scope.description: All tracked repository content and paths evaluated by the fixed forbidden-reference patterns.

evidence_requirements: A bounded match count and normalized references without raw matched content.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking executor in Issue #8.

rules.title: Maintained JavaScript must have zero approved lint errors
rules.description: The package-owned Node adapter must report zero diagnostics configured as errors; warnings remain informational.

scope.description: Tracked maintained JavaScript selected by the approved node-v1 adapter.

evidence_requirements: Bounded diagnostic counts with analyzer identity and version.

approval.rationale: Approved as a blocking Engineering Quality Profile v1 condition in Issue #9.

rules.title: Classic cyclomatic complexity must not exceed 15 per function
rules.description: Every maintained JavaScript function must have classic McCabe cyclomatic complexity at or below 15.

scope.description: Each function in tracked maintained JavaScript selected by node-v1.

evidence_requirements: Bounded file, symbol, measured value, threshold, analyzer identity, and version.

approval.rationale: Approved with maximum complexity 15 in Issue #9.

rules.title: The required unit suite must complete without skipped or todo tests
rules.description: The node-v1 unit suite must exist, discover and execute tests, contain no skipped or todo tests, and complete successfully.

scope.description: Tracked tests classified under test/unit/**/*.test.js.

evidence_requirements: Machine-readable discovered, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and todo counts.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking suite in Issue #9.

rules.title: The required integration suite must complete without skipped or todo tests
rules.description: The node-v1 integration suite must exist, discover and execute tests, contain no skipped or todo tests, and complete successfully.

scope.description: Tracked tests classified under test/integration/**/*.test.js.

evidence_requirements: Machine-readable discovered, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and todo counts.

approval.rationale: Approved as a required blocking suite in Issue #9.

rules.title: Combined production coverage must meet repository-wide thresholds
rules.description: Combined unit and integration coverage must meet exact repository-wide thresholds for lines, branches, functions, and statements.

scope.description: Combined coverage over tracked bin/**/*.js and src/**/*.js production code.

evidence_requirements: Exact covered and total counts for all four coverage dimensions.

approval.rationale: Approved with global thresholds in Issue #9.

rules.title: Changed and new production code must meet enhanced coverage thresholds
rules.description: Instrumentable changed or new production locations must meet exact changed-code thresholds relative to an explicit immutable comparison commit.

scope.description: Instrumentable production locations intersecting changed lines relative to the effective merge base.

evidence_requirements: Supplied and effective base SHAs plus exact applicable, covered, and total counts.

approval.rationale: Approved with changed-code thresholds in Issue #9.

rules.title: Production JavaScript modules must not contain dependency cycles
rules.description: The node-v1 production module graph must contain no circular dependency.

scope.description: Tracked JavaScript modules under bin/ and src/.

evidence_requirements: Bounded normalized dependency-cycle paths.

approval.rationale: Approved as an objective architecture boundary in Issue #9.

rules.title: Production code must not depend on test code
rules.description: JavaScript under bin/ or src/ must not import modules under test/.

scope.description: Tracked production JavaScript under bin/ and src/.

evidence_requirements: Bounded normalized source and forbidden dependency locations.

approval.rationale: Approved as an objective architecture boundary in Issue #9.

rules.title: Source modules must not depend on CLI entry points
rules.description: JavaScript under src/ must not import modules under bin/.

scope.description: Tracked JavaScript under src/.

evidence_requirements: Bounded normalized src-to-bin dependency locations.

approval.rationale: Approved as an objective architecture boundary in Issue #9.

rules.title: Production imports must resolve reliably
rules.description: Every production JavaScript import must resolve under the pinned package-owned architecture analyzer.

scope.description: Tracked JavaScript imports under bin/ and src/.

evidence_requirements: Bounded normalized unresolved import locations and analyzer version.

approval.rationale: Approved as an objective architecture boundary in Issue #9.

rules.title: Production code must not import development-only dependencies
rules.description: JavaScript under bin/ or src/ must not import a package declared only in devDependencies.

scope.description: Tracked JavaScript imports under bin/ and src/ plus package dependency declarations.

evidence_requirements: Bounded normalized production imports linked to development-only dependency declarations.

approval.rationale: Approved as an objective architecture boundary in Issue #9.

rules.title: Material ambiguity should be clarified before implementation
rules.description: Architecture, persistence, API, business logic, and UX assumptions with material alternatives should be surfaced for a human decision.

scope.description: Implementation work with materially ambiguous outcomes.

evidence_requirements: The material alternatives and the recorded human decision.

rules.title: Implement the minimum solution that satisfies the approved request
rules.description: Avoid speculative features, unused flexibility, and abstractions that do not serve the approved capability.

scope.description: All implementation changes.

evidence_requirements: Changed lines traced to approved acceptance criteria.

rules.title: Changes should remain surgical
rules.description: Only files and lines required for the approved capability should change, while unrelated user work remains intact.

scope.description: Repository modifications made by an implementation task.

evidence_requirements: A scoped diff with unrelated edits excluded.

rules.title: Execution should use explicit verifiable goals
rules.description: Implementation steps should state observable success criteria and loop until those checks pass or a real blocker is reported.

scope.description: Multi-step repository changes.

evidence_requirements: A plan with a verification criterion for each step.

rules.title: Structural code questions should prefer CodeGraph
rules.description: Symbol definitions, callers, callees, impact, and structural context should use the repository graph when initialized.

scope.description: Structural repository reconnaissance when CodeGraph is available.

evidence_requirements: The graph query used or a recorded reason it was unavailable.
